A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDSM dataset and AMD framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix; v2 includes readable appendices A–M.

before.justification: Tables 2–4 report original MDSM/DGM4 experiments, component ablations and evaluations across narrative-generating MLLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original human evaluation, controlled comparisons, transfer experiments, ablations and failure analyses.

M1.justification: AMD retains artifact tokens, frozen pre-perception encoding, manipulation-oriented reasoning, auxiliary losses, TRP and textual inference. The fuller prompts and dataset-construction descriptions document existing procedures rather than establish a changed method. Diffusion and non-alignment variants serve as experimental conditions.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands beyond MDSM and DGM4 to COSMOS, MiRAGe, DiFF and DiffFace, plus diffusion-based face editing, background modification and full-image generation (Appendices H–I). v2 also evaluates missing-modality and non-aligned inputs and introduces a human participant study.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B and -7B comparisons on MDSM; v1 evaluated Qwen2.5-VL only zero-shot. This is a focused comparator addition. The original ViLT, HAMMER, HAMMER++, FKA-Owl and zero-shot comparator rows remain.

E3.justification: New designs include a 100-pair study with 15 volunteers, size-matched dataset comparisons including a 103k-sample Guardian subset, cross-dataset transfer, and two-epoch LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen models (Appendices A, C, G–J). Newly disclosed settings for the retained AMD experiments do not establish that their protocols changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and cross-MLLM analyses, v2 tests token length, knowledge-preservation strategies, TRP placement, modality removal and semantic alignment. It adds corpus analysis, diffusion robustness tests, token visualizations and concrete failure cases (Tables 5–8 and 11–15; Figures 5 and 11–14).

E5.justification: Appendix K.2 newly specifies averaging token representations over 100 samples per group, with three independent groups per manipulation class, to reduce sampling randomness. This is limited statistical aggregation for visualizations. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds extensive outcomes in Tables 5–15 and new figures. For example, Table 9 reports 72.00 average ACC for NYT-trained Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and Table 10 reports AMD's 54.08 average cross-dataset ACC. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements to the original scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–10 are retained, including attention pooling, auxiliary objectives and TRP. The appendices add empirical analyses and metric explanations, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a semantically aligned MLLM-generated misinformation benchmark and an efficient AMD framework for detection, grounding and generalization. v2 adds numerical highlights to the abstract and contribution list, but these substantiate retained claims rather than introduce a different core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies dataset difficulty through size-controlled comparisons, explains limited transfer to untampered but mismatched COSMOS pairs, and discusses persistent FA&TF/TF failures and possible retrieval-based remedies (Appendices C, H and M). This substantially expands the interpretation beyond v1's brief celebrity-face scope limitation and general performance discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E add full prompts, coordinate conventions, baseline adaptations, hardware, image preprocessing, batch size, optimizer, learning-rate schedule and training duration. Appendix L documents head-shot sourcing and filtering. v1 supplied mainly the backbone, frozen encoder and token count. Both versions still promise future code release.

R1.justification: Related work adds a focused comparison with MMFakeBench and elaborates FKA-Owl's task and computational limitations. Supporting references expand to diffusion benchmarks, corpus tools, visualization and celebrity resources. The principal positioning around semantically aligned, MLLM-driven misinformation remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the explanatory material: dataset construction is rewritten by manipulation category, related work is expanded, quantitative discussion is condensed, and experimental setup moves into a structured A–M appendix with a contents list. The method and conclusion remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised and placed before the abstract, Figure 2 is extensively redrawn, and Table 1 gains a dataset row and training-support column. New Figures 5–14 and Tables 5–15 add visualizations, comparisons and cases, substantially expanding the presentation beyond relocation or numerical edits.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked human validation, evaluation beyond MDSM/DGM4 and substantial reproduction details. v2 addresses these gaps with human evaluation, size and alignment controls, fine-tuned comparators, transfer tests, failure analysis and detailed prompts/settings. These additions substantially strengthen empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. Some new reporting is imprecise—for example, Appendix G calls Table 9's domain-average accuracies in-domain—and performance uncertainty remains unquantified, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains.
